message: Include the TALK-BACK block and a valid PROMISE line before spawning a helper.
A finished helper cannot be resumed; start a fresh helper with a Delta.
Re-anchor the current request with the run goal, open items and owner rules.

A ledger tick counts only with a recorded verdict (the hivecall_verdict tool, or a BB result's exact `VERDICT ISC-n <verdict>` line): APPROVE_CODE, or APPROVE_PLAN or SELECTED for Discovery items only from a helper verified as the reviewer agent (native subagent agent=reviewer, or a BB thread whose brief has an `agent: reviewer` line, pinned by its own command `printf '%s' '{"threadId":"<id>","agent":"reviewer","queued":false}' | bb plugin rpc call --input-file /dev/stdin opencode stampAgent` that printed {"ok": true}), or REPRODUCED or PASS from a verified qa helper for Discovery items only, or a verified qa PASS whose brief names the receipt commit when that commit only renames files or changes tests or docs on a proven parent (run base or checkpoint, or a ticked item's receipt commit), plus a commit id that exists in this checkout and an existing evidence file.

Do not close the run or write the final report while counted ledger items are open or ticked without approval and receipt. Save ledger updates in a separate completed tool call before closing. To park an unproven HTML item, leave its checkbox unticked, add data-status="parked" to that item's input, and append a BLOCKED result with the reason and unlock condition (references/kickoff.md, Parking an item). A box that stays ticked without approval and receipt can be closed over only after three pauses and once the run card lists it on a `Not counted: ISC-x` line, so the owner sees it was not counted. A close with any parked item is held until the run card says `Goal met: no - parked: ISC-x, ...` naming every parked id, as the first line of the final report.
Two REVISE_CODE results on this slice mean split it or change angle; do not send a third fix brief.

Hill climb: helpers keep finishing on this with no new tick. Reflect, then adapt (HOW-TO-WORK.md, Progress): put a block in the next brief — `RE-PLAN item=<id|run>`, `Tried: <what the last attempts did>`, `Evidence: <existing file showing what was learned>`, `Next: new angle <how it differs> | split <into what> | park <unlock>` — never wider scope or a lower bar.

Work off deltas: these items already passed and nothing changed since their receipt commits, so review or QA would redo valid work. Pick an open item, or add a `WHY:` line saying what this run can learn that the last pass did not.
The judge stays apart: a qa brief names the exact commit it tests, so its PASS is about one candidate. Add the commit id, or a `WHY:` line if this check is not about code.
QA must test the named commit in its own clean copy (a worktree); edits in this checkout are not part of that candidate.
Right agent for the job: review work runs as agent=reviewer and qa work as agent=qa, so the judge is the agent built for it. Respawn with that agent.
